newsitem.title: UK: UK's MFI optimistic on January sale.
newsitem.headline: UK's MFI optimistic on January sale.

text.p: Britain's leading furniture retailer and manufacturer MFI Furniture Group Plc on Monday said it was optimistic about its key January/February sale, and that the benefits of a housing upturn were still to come.

"We're looking at January with a high degree of confidence," chairman Derek Hunt told a news conference. The group's traditional January sale, which starts on December 26, accounts for 30 percent of annual turnover.

The group attributed its 63 percent first half profit increase to improved consumer confidence rather than a housing market revival. MFI thinks the housing market is still sluggish, and that the benefits from an upturn still lie ahead.

"We think the housing market is still dormant," chief executive John Randall told a news conference, saying that the upturn in sales and profits had come from increased consumer confidence and the more buoyant economy. He said the housing market outside the south east of the country had not really changed.
Gross margins, which improved by just over two percentage points, also helped profits.

Randall said the group had seen a reduction in raw material prices, which had gone up dramatically in 1994. He said they were still above 1994 levels, but seemed to have reached a plateau for the moment.
MFI spent 37 million pounds during the first half, including 15 million on transforming its MFI stores into new-style MFI Homeworks, which carry a wider range of goods.
Hunt said these new format stores were producing a double figure sales uplift. The group has converted 78 of its 184 UK stores and expects it will take two more years to convert the entire chain.
Capital expenditure for the year as a whole is expected to be 70 million pounds, up from 60 million in the previous year. Spending in 1997/98 is likely to stay around the 70 million pound level.

Its new Howden Joinery business, which is not yet in profit, is trading from 24 depots and there are plans to double the number of warehouses in the next year. Hunt said MFI saw the potential for about 200 outlets eventually.
